article.articleHeadline: Jumantik volunteers in Mampang Prapatan receive dengue prevention education.
article.articleSummary: 100 Jumantik volunteers from five sub-districts in Mampang Prapatan, South Jakarta, received dengue prevention education as part of a collaboration between Puskesmas Mampang Prapatan and Soffell, with support from Enesis Group, during the Kampung Bebas Jentik (KBJ) contest at the Kecamatan level. Held at the Mampang Prapatan District Office hall, the event aims to mobilize residents to monitor and control mosquito larvae via a community- and family-based environmental approach. Education focused on protection from mosquito bites and personal protective measures, with Enesis providing products and guidance on self-protection. Practices highlighted include 3M (drain, cover, recycle) and applying mosquito repellent, promoting sustained preventive behavior to keep environments free of breeding sites and reduce dengue transmission. The article does not report any outbreak data or case counts.

article.articleHeadline: Tanjungpinang City Government Integrates CKG Services and TB Tracing at 87 Locations, Check the Locations!
article.articleSummary: Tanjungpinang City, in Indonesia’s Riau Islands Province, integrates Free Health Check-Ups (CKG) with tuberculosis (TB) tracing at 87 locations, targeting 100 people per site from September 9 to November 27, 2026. Rustam, head of the Health, Population Control and Family Planning Agency (Dinkesdalduk KB), said the program covers free health examinations, TB screening, sputum collection, and chest X-rays. The initiative also launches the Gasak TB movement (Gerakan Antar Warga Periksa TB) to mobilize residents to refer and screen symptomatic or high-risk individuals. An estimated 1,800 TB cases occur annually in Tanjungpinang, but only about 24% have been detected so far. CKD coverage stands at roughly 45,000 of a 120,000-target by year end, with monthly screenings totaling 800–1,000 people. Door-to-door tracing by health cadres aims to accelerate early detection and treatment, reducing transmission; TB is curable with proper therapy. Indonesia targets TB-free status by 2030.

article.articleHeadline: Central Java Health Office Chief Suspects MBG Poisoning Was Caused by Water Quality Contaminated with E. coli
article.articleSummary: As of September 9, 2026, Central Java's Health Office Chief suspects water quality contaminated with Escherichia coli as the likely cause of a wave of MBG poisoning in the East Pantura region of Central Java. Zulfachmi Wahab said the same source has appeared in other MBG poisoning cases in Java. He urged BGN Java to upgrade water filtration across all SPPG facilities to prevent contaminated water used in MBG preparation. He rejected claims that outbreaks stem from SPPG lacking the Sertifikat Laik Higiene Sanitasi (SLHS), noting the facilities reportedly hold SLHS documents; still, SLHS remains a key standard for cleanliness. MBG poisoning is multifactorial—environmental sanitation, handler hygiene, and water quality—with E. coli as a primary risk. Lab confirmation will take about one to two weeks, and the exact cause remains unclear.

The cause is under investigation and not yet confirmed as MBG-related; possible bacterial or viral contamination is considered, with laboratory results pending. article.articleHeadline: Three Types of Bacteria Cause a Karo Student to Suffer MBG Poisoning, a Female Student with Memory Impairment Undergoes a Trauma Test

The implicated samples were MBG brought to the school, not sourced from the kitchen, though standard retention procedures (1×24 hours or 2×24 hours) were referenced. A female student, Febiona, reported memory impairment and is part of a Kasus Luar Biasa (KLB) investigation. Lab head Pulo Rizal Togatorop emphasized contamination or handling issues as potential causes, with ongoing efforts to trace the outbreak source and confirm the bacteria. Geography: Karo, North Sumatra, Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: The History of Ancol Reclamation: Former Wetlands That Were Malaria Breeding Grounds
article.articleSummary: Ancol, in North Jakarta, was historically marshland known as a malaria mosquito breeding ground. By the 1960s the area remained swampy and malaria-prone, prompting a shift toward tourism development. Dutch East Indies Governor Adriaan Valckenier first eyed Ancol for potential tourist development in the early 17th century, but realisation was delayed by priorities and independence-era conflicts. In December 1965, President Sukarno ordered and appointed Governor H. Soemarno Sosroatmodjo to lead the project. Beginning in 1966, Ancol's redevelopment proceeded through land reclamation and filling to transform the malaria-prone wetlands into a major Jakarta tourism and recreation district.

article.articleHeadline: Low risk of the Congo Ebola outbreak entering China; the Ministry of Health continues to monitor closely.
article.articleSummary: China regards the risk of cross-border importation of Ebola from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as currently low, per Senior Health Minister Chen Jiehao. There are no direct flights between DRC and China, and traveler volume is limited, reducing import risk. Ebola Virus Disease spreads mainly through direct contact with infected bodily fluids. The ongoing DRC outbreak has been driven by delayed case detection and inadequate infection control in communities and healthcare facilities; yet in well-resourced settings like Singapore, transmission is not easy. China will maintain vigilance, monitoring Ebola and other deadly pathogens worldwide, and adjust measures if the situation changes. Measures in place include enhanced surveillance and electronic health declarations for inbound travellers, with healthcare workers trained to stay alert. With year-end school holidays travel peak approaching, authorities will continue to monitor and may strengthen screening for travellers from certain countries as needed.

A DRC delegation arrived at Karuziika Palace to pay tribute but was screened; none showed Ebola symptoms and remained under active surveillance. Uganda declared the 2026 outbreak ended on July 28 after a 42-day period following discharge of the last confirmed patient on July 16. The outbreak originated in May in DRC and was epidemiologically linked to DRC transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Bukedi's bitter-sweet battle against malaria
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Uganda's Bukedi Sub-region shows a turnaround. Butebo District's malaria positivity declined from about 60% in 2021 to 25–35% after expanded indoor residual spraying, insecticide-treated nets, and test-and-treat; 14 health facilities operate there, with drug stocks secure and active community outreach. Kibuku District's burden fell from 850 to 266 per 1,000; drugs are redistributed to Kiboga, Mukono, Kiryadongo, Bukedea, and Mbale. District health officials credit household-level prevention and leader advocacy. Budaka District has 52% positivity, reporting 5,671 cases in June (67%) and 7,921 in July (69%), with 5,000–8,000 weekly cases; facility deaths at 2–3 per week, communities 3–4 per week. Blood shortages persist (30–40 units/month needed, about one-third donated). Emphasis remains on test, treat, and bed nets.

article.articleHeadline: How a Driver's Sudden Death Triggered Ebola Panic in Congo
article.articleSummary: Marabo village, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo, confronted Ebola panic as a truck driver died with heavy bleeding shortly after repair of a burst tire, raising fears of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak that has killed more than 2,500 people in roughly 100 days. A dispute over burial rights with colleagues and a decision by the village chief delayed release of the body, highlighting challenges to contact tracing when families resist authorities. Rapid on-site testing by WHO-linked laboratories returned negative for Ebola, though experts warn false negatives are possible. The case underscores ongoing containment challenges in Ituri and the need for cautious handling of suspected victims.

article.articleHeadline: Emergency Funding Alone is Insufficient to End Bundibugyo virus
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with cross-border transmission into Uganda highlights critical gaps in global medical countermeasures and financing. Despite accelerating development and deployment of diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics and PPE by Africa CDC, WHO, manufacturers, researchers and financing partners, funding remains slow and heavily dependent on emergency mobilisation. The outbreak exposes lack of predictable, sustainable financing and routine systems to develop, manufacture, procure, stockpile and rapidly deploy MCMs before crises occur. Key gaps include absence of near-point-of-care BDBV diagnostics, fragmented PPE markets, limited decentralised manufacturing and weak purchasing power in affected regions. Authors—including Victor J Dzau, Jean Kaseya, Benedict O. Oramah and John-Arne Røttingen—urge governments to act on G20 High Level Independent Panel recommendations for financing the global commons to control the current Ebola outbreak and to prepare for future threats such as Ebola and Marburg.

article.articleHeadline: Balloon Juice - Plagues & Pandemics Update - September 9, 2026
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo tops 6,600 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths since it was declared a global health emergency in mid-May, marking the fastest-moving Ebola outbreak. In the United States, COVID-19 weekly deaths peaked at about 26,000 in 2021 and 484 per week in 2026; as of Sept 2, 2026, 47 states show growing infections, with no declines. In Canada, COVID-19 activity is currently moderate overall, with British Columbia and several eastern provinces at higher levels and Alberta/Saskatchewan at lower levels. It also supports hygiene and sanitation: distributing hygiene kits, improving water access in health facilities, and constructing hygienic latrines, with nine school kit trucks to be distributed soon. CRS provides food support to patients and families and psychosocial care to address trauma. Funded by the U.S. government through the State Department, the project covers Ituri, Wamba, Mambasa, Mahagi and now extends to Tshopo, starting in June and continuing as long as needed; CRS will stay engaged in Ituri with other emergency response projects.

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19: The mystery unfolds
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 origin mystery persists as of 2026-09-09, driven by legal and scientific debates. A guilty plea by Dr. David Morens, adviser to Dr. Fauci, to conspiring to defraud the US government involved using personal emails to hide federal records, including discussions of bat coronavirus research tied to a Wuhan, China lab. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment in congressional hearings; the House panel voted to hold him in contempt. The Lancet declined an inquiry’s request for internal records. Ashish Jha shifted to favor an accidental lab leak at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. The White House endorsed lab-leak theory; WHO and independent researchers say origins remain unresolved, though data and market-linked species like raccoon dogs support natural spillover; furin cleavage site cited. The global virus continues; the Stratus (XFG) variant drives waves. US deaths surpass 1.1 million; Germany ~2,000 per million; Canada under 1,400 per million. Calls for rigorous, evidence-based inquiry amid political rhetoric.

article.articleHeadline: Man with neck swelling that wouldn't heal diagnosed with cat scratch disease—petting cats to blame
article.articleSummary: A 43-year-old man from Henan, China, developed a progressively enlarging cervical mass. Surgical pathology showed granulomatous inflammation with positive PPD and T-SPOT, initially leading to a diagnosis of lymph node tuberculosis. At Wuhan Pulmonary Hospital, Dr. Yang Chengqing elicited cat exposure—patient had contact with wild cats—and the physician recalled a previous similar case ultimately diagnosed as cat scratch disease. Biopsy testing confirmed Bartonella henselae infection. After targeted treatment, the patient rapidly improved. Cat scratch disease typically features stellate necrotizing granulomas with microabscesses. Transmission is flea-borne: cats harbor Bartonella henselae and transmit infection to humans when flea-contaminated material enters a scratch or bite. Immunocompetent individuals often recover spontaneously; fever or severe pain warrants medical care. Preventive advice includes flea-control for cats, avoiding direct handling, thorough wound washing with soap after scratches or bites, and reporting cat exposure to clinicians.

article.articleHeadline: Often drinks unboiled mountain spring water; a Guangxi woman has a five-centimeter-long live worm in her brain.
article.articleSummary: In Guangxi, China, a 56-year-old woman who habitually drank untreated stream and mountain spring water developed cerebral sparganosis. She presented with facial asymmetry, slurred speech, and progressive limb weakness, and was misdiagnosed for years as stroke or brain tumor before imaging and CSF analyses confirmed an intracranial parasite infection in 2019. Despite conservative treatment, headaches and numbness worsened. In 2026, Guangzhou surgeons performed an awake craniotomy to remove a live sparganum about 5 cm long from her brain, enabling real-time monitoring of language and motor function during extraction; postoperatively, her limb strength and speech improved markedly. The case underscores the risk from drinking untreated surface water. Authorities advise boiling mountain spring water and rivers before drinking and separating raw from cooked foods to prevent sparganosis.

article.articleHeadline: Diarrhea on an overseas business trip mistaken for acclimatization; back home, a sudden acute illness leads to hospitalization. Doctor: Typhoid fever has a long incubation period and is easily confused with a common cold.
article.articleSummary: Imported typhoid fever in a 37-year-old Chinese business traveler returning from Bangladesh to Zhejiang. Last month he experienced daily diarrhea (3–5 times) and transient fever, self-treated with antipyretics. After returning home he developed persistent fever, myalgia, headache, dry throat, abdominal distension, and mild upper abdominal pain. At Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital, splenomegaly and low eosinophils prompted suspicion of enteric fever; blood culture confirmed Salmonella Typhi infection. After standard anti-infective and supportive therapy, fever resolved and he recovered fully. The report underscores that enteric fever has a long incubation (1–3 weeks) and can mimic common cold or gastroenteritis, risking misdiagnosis with self-medication. Prevention for travelers includes safe drinking water, fully cooked foods, strict hand hygiene, and post-travel observation for 2–4 weeks.

article.articleHeadline: CMS: Initial Prescriptions for Silevimig Injection, the World's First Bispecific Antibody Against Rabies, Issued in China
article.articleSummary: As of Sept 9, 2026, CMS announced initial prescriptions for Silevimig Injection, the world’s first fully human bispecific antibody for passive rabies immunization, issued across multiple Chinese hospitals including Beijing Luhe Hospital, Wenzhou People’s Hospital, Kaiping Central Hospital, Dongguan Guangji Hospital, and Huidong Jilong Ankang Hospital, marking large‑scale clinical use. The product targets dual rabies G protein epitopes I and III, enabling immediate neutralization of diverse strains and protection before vaccine-induced immunity develops. It uses a 0.05 mg/kg dose, with smaller injection volume than HRIG, is non-plasma-derived, scalable, and designed to improve safety and patient compliance. Approved for marketing in June 2026; initial prescriptions occurred about two months post-approval via Genrix Bio. Rabies remains nearly 100% fatal once symptomatic; standard post-exposure management combines vaccination and passive immunization. In China, over 40 million exposures annually, about 40% Category III, with only ~15% receiving passive immunization.

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza hits France again: Why 7,600 ducks had to die—and what that means for foie gras.
article.articleSummary: As of 9 September 2026, France reports an H5N1 avian influenza outbreak at a farm in Longué-Jumelles, Maine-et-Loire, prompting culling of more than 7,600 mulard ducks. A 10-km zone restricts poultry movements to curb spread. The incident strains the foie gras sector, which relies primarily on ducks (about 98% of production) and has faced large-scale culling in 2022/23. Cities including Bordeaux, Lyon, Montpellier and Pessac have removed foie gras from official events over welfare concerns. Santé publique France says foie gras is not a human health risk, as heat treatment destroys the virus. Ducks can be asymptomatic carriers, making them “Trojan horses” for H5N1. The outbreak arrives amid rising Chinese competition, which now accounts for a substantial share of world foie gras. France’s 2023 vaccination program reduces risk but, with a ~20-day dosing gap, about 50–55% of ducks remain unvaccinated; the recent flock had first but not second doses.

article.articleHeadline: AI Spots Foodborne Threats Before They Spread
article.articleSummary: Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce from Mexico triggers >6,000 confirmed cases across 15 states, hundreds hospitalized, and two deaths as of 2026-09-09. AI-enabled systems quickly flag anomalies and trace supply chains, augmenting traditional surveillance (patient reports, lab confirmations, traceback interviews) by scanning pharmacy sales, search trends, social media, and electronic health records in near real time to trigger alerts ahead of formal notices. Lab advances include ARUP Laboratories’ AI with Techcyte using a convolutional neural network on stool slides to speed initial screening, with final confirmation by staff; conventional confirmation can take weeks. Tianjin University’s Raman spectroscopy with machine learning achieves 98.4% accuracy for pathogen serotypes and 99.2% in mixed samples. Prevention efforts include USDA-funded Salmonella-onions screening, NSF-supported AI tools in Hawaii, and the EU TraceMap supply-chain platform; data quality, confidentiality, and human oversight remain key limits.

article.articleHeadline: Andes hantavirus: quarantine in France after an imported case from South America.
article.articleSummary: France quarantined 45 high-risk contacts after an imported Andes hantavirus case from South America. A young Franco-Argentinian developed symptoms on return and tested positive for Andes virus, a hantavirus with documented human-to-human transmission. Santé publique France placed the 45 exposed individuals under quarantine; a decree dated 7 August 2026 enables isolation of confirmed cases and quarantine of exposed contacts, reflecting enhanced legal tools for emerging infections. Incubation is typically 1–6 weeks; Andes virus can cause hantavirus pulmonary syndrome with case fatality exceeding 30% in South American series, with no specific antiviral or widely available vaccine. The article also notes ALTNV—Asian longhorned tick nairovirus—identified in febrile patients with tick exposure in China; ALTNV is an orthonairovirus, not an orthohantavirus, illustrating different reservoirs and vectors. This case tests France's ability to isolate, trace, and regulate rare, transmissible viruses.

article.articleHeadline: Quarantine Headquarters hosts workshop on animal disease diagnosis and antibiotic resistance with participation from 12 Asia-Pacific countries.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-09-10, Korea's Quarantine Headquarters organized two international trainings with 12 Asia-Pacific countries: the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) standard laboratory animal disease diagnosis workshop and the joint APAC veterinary antimicrobial resistance technology training. Now in its 13th year (since 2012), the workshop covered eight major animal diseases—including foot-and-mouth disease, avian influenza, rabies, and brucellosis—through theory and hands-on sessions. Participants reviewed shared diagnostic capabilities, notably the quarantine service’s on-site foot-and-mouth disease molecular diagnostic system. The antimicrobial resistance module covered the full workflow from bacterial isolation and identification to antibiotic susceptibility testing, result interpretation, and surveillance use. Korea’s quarantine head Choi Jung-rok said the program will sustain international cooperation and strengthen global veterinary public health using Korea’s diagnostic and surveillance technologies in collaboration with WOAH.

article.articleSummary: China's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs confirmed an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease serotype O in pigs at a slaughter facility in Dazu District, Chongqing Municipality, in southwest China. Beijing said the report originated from the Chinese Center for Animal Disease Prevention and Control on Tuesday, 8 September. The affected facility housed 677 pigs, 37 of which exhibited clinical signs consistent with foot-and-mouth disease. In response, local authorities immediately activated comprehensive emergency measures, including culling of affected animals, thorough disinfection, safe disposal of carcasses, and enhanced swine surveillance and screening, complemented by an epidemiological investigation, the ministry stated immediately publicly.

Hosted by the Lianxi District Health Commission and executed by the district CDC's schistosomiasis division, the program covered key points in disease screening, case recognition, information reporting requirements, and infection-lab procedures, with hands-on lab practicals to assess proficiency. Clinicians reviewed case identification criteria, infectious disease reporting timelines, and referral workflows, aiming to strengthen early discovery, rapid reporting, and prompt case management. The district will maintain ongoing training, supervision, and guidance to standardize full-cycle surveillance and advance an early detection, early alert, early response approach, thereby safeguarding the district's schistosomiasis elimination achievements and residents' health.

article.articleSummary: Hand-foot-mouth disease is rising in Lam Dong province, Vietnam. In the four weeks before September 2, Lam Dong recorded 3,871 HFMD cases since January 1, including two deaths in Ta Nang commune and the Duc Trong area. Cases are up about 2,100 versus the same period in 2025. The outbreak now spans 121 of 124 communes; hotspots include Phan Thiet, Da Lat, Duc Trong, La Gi, and Ham Thuan Bac. Children under 5 are most affected, with 87.3% of cases in nurseries and kindergartens. On September 7, the Lam Dong People’s Committee issued a directive to prevent HFMD and other infectious diseases in schools, urging stronger coordination and rapid containment. The Education Department and local authorities will train teachers, caregivers, and school health staff; schools must ensure well-ventilated, clean classrooms, apply the 3 clean principle, monitor health, and promptly report suspected cases to health authorities.

article.articleHeadline: CDC updates global travel notice as incurable virus reaches America
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever, a mosquito-borne, incurable illness, prompted the CDC to issue a Level 1 global travel advisory as of 2026-09-09, as cases rise and reach the United States. Twelve countries—Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Kenya, Bangladesh, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Malaysia, Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, and Vietnam—show higher-than-expected dengue risk for travelers. In the contiguous U.S., 346 travel-associated and 73 locally acquired cases have been reported, including 72 in Florida and 1 in Virginia. A 2024 CDC report recorded 3,798 dengue cases nationwide (97% travel-associated, 3% local), with 36% hospitalized and six deaths; cases rose 359% versus the 2010–2023 average. Dengue is present in more than 100 countries and caused a 2025 Americas outbreak in Brazil approaching 200,000 cases. Symptoms begin 5–7 days after infection and include fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, musculoskeletal pain, and gum bleeding. No cure; treatment is supportive. A three-dose vaccine for ages 9–16 reduces symptomatic infection by ~80%.

article.articleHeadline: Ha Tinh Takes Proactive Measures to Prevent and Control Foot-and-Mouth Disease in Livestock.

SAT1 serotype is spreading globally; domestic herds lack immunity. Ha Tinh exceeds 590,000 livestock. Continued surveillance, market and transport controls, and vaccination are emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: Interview: What WHO's Revised Kala-Azar Guidelines Mean For India
article.articleSummary: WHO, in July 2026, issued revised guidelines for kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) and its skin manifestation PKDL, reducing miltefosine use due to ocular toxicity and teratogenic risks. The guidelines also address relapse after liposomal amphotericin B and discontinue sodium stibogluconate injections in Africa. PKDL affects about 5-10% of treated Kala-azar patients and can sustain transmission since affected individuals harbor the parasite; this underpins elimination efforts in India and neighboring regions. The guidelines emphasize considering health-system context, contraceptive availability, nutrition, and rights of vulnerable patients. India reached its Kala-azar elimination target in 2023 (less than 10 cases per block per 10,000) and entered a three-year consolidation phase; Bangladesh was validated in 2023. The interview with Shyam Sundar of Banaras Hindu University and Muzaffarpur’s Kala-azar Medical Research Centre discusses relapse management, miltefosine safety, and practical treatment choices, noting Sundar’s Padma Shri honor in May 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Think it's food poisoning? The infection could reach your brain
article.articleSummary: India’s monsoon heightens risks of brain infections from unsafe food and water, per Dr. Manjari Tripathi (AIIMS). Taenia solium eggs contaminate leafy greens and other produce; ingestion of raw or undercooked foods allows eggs to reach the brain and form cysts (neurocysticercosis). Cysts can calcify and trigger seizures, headaches, brain swelling, vomiting, and sometimes cognitive decline; multiple cysts may create a “starry sky” brain image. Transmission also occurs via poorly cooked pork or contaminated food and water; thorough cooking kills eggs and scrubbing produce under running water is advised. Monsoon stagnation raises leptospirosis risk (encephalopathy, kidney failure) and mosquito-borne dengue/dengue encephalitis with seizures or brain bleeding; mosquitoes breed in standing water. Seek evaluation within 24 hours for severe headache with fever and vomiting. Prevention emphasizes vaccines and vector-control measures.

Purulent meningitis is rare but serious; urgent medical care is essential if suspected.

article.articleHeadline: Leprosy: what it is, symptoms, and how it is transmitted.
article.articleSummary: Leprosy, or Hansen's disease, is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, a slow-growing bacterium. Although ancient civilizations in China, Egypt, and India feared it as incurable and contagious, leprosy is now readily diagnosed and curable with antibiotic therapy. Transmission requires close, prolonged contact; airborne spread via nasal secretions or saliva may occur, but most exposed individuals do not develop disease. Those with weakened immunity, e.g., chronic illnesses like diabetes, are at higher risk. Early signs include hypopigmented or erythematous skin lesions that heal poorly, sensory loss (numbness to touch, heat, or pain), and muscle weakness. Nerve, bone, joints, and muscle damage can progress; nodules (lepromas) and plaques may appear. Incubation averages 5–7 years, ranging from months to 10 years. MDT (multi-drug therapy) became freely available via WHO in 1995, reducing global incidence; elimination efforts target remaining endemic countries and sub-national levels.

article.articleHeadline: Pamela Anderson Was Told She Had 10 Years To Live: What Is Hepatitis C And Can It Be Cured?
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis C is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmitted through infected blood and often asymptomatic for years. Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) now cure more than 95% of cases, with fewer side effects and pangenotypic regimens. This contrasts with the interferon era, when treatment was long, toxic, and less effective. Pamela Anderson was diagnosed in the late 1990s after sharing a tattoo needle with her then-husband Tommy Lee and was told she had about ten years to live; she later declared herself hepatitis C-free in 2015. Diagnosis requires HCV RNA testing to confirm active infection, not just antibodies. While curing the virus halts ongoing damage, advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis may persist, keeping cancer risk and the need for surveillance. Transmission remains blood-borne, with sexual spread possible but less common. In India, Amrita Hospital's Dr. Mahendra Rajput notes SVR >95% with DAAs.

Veterinary expert Dr. Ram Ottalwar urges farmers to monitor animals for fever, weakness, and reduced appetite and to apply appropriate control measures. Prevention combines medications, sprays, soaps, tablets, and injections used under veterinary guidance, and attention to ticks in environments such as wall cracks and vegetation. article.articleHeadline: Counterfeit Abhayrab rabies vaccine sparks fresh health alert

Legitimate Abhayrab stocks released under Certificate CDL/2025/8392 (Nov 7, 2025) are safe and distributed through authorized channels. Anyone who received Abhayrab on or after Nov 7, 2025 should verify their vaccination history with a healthcare professional; scan the vial QR code to confirm authenticity. Vaccines must be given intramuscularly or intradermally in the thighs or shoulders; injections in the buttocks are invalid and must be repeated. A 10-day rule applies for dog/cat bites; rabies remains nearly 100% fatal, underscoring urgency. This marks a second major Abhayrab counterfeit scare in India, following KA24014 alerted by ATAGI in Australia.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Season: Don't Make These Mistakes When Using Repellents to Protect Yourself from Mosquito Bites.
article.articleSummary: On 9 September 2026, dengue surveillance was intensified in Chennai and Pune. Dermatologists advise EPA-approved repellents containing DEET, Picaridin, or Oil of Lemon Eucalyptus (OLE). Use on exposed skin and clothing; sunscreen first, then repellent; avoid combined products, and reapply sunscreen every two hours if outdoors. Daytime Aedes bites peak 8–10 am and 3–5 pm, so take precautions during travel. Repellent duration: 10% DEET ~2 hours; 30% DEET ~5 hours; 20% Picaridin up to 8 hours. Do not use OLE or PMD on children under 3; under 2 months should not use repellents. Pregnant women may use DEET or Picaridin as directed. For children, have an adult apply repellent on their hands first, then to the child’s face; avoid eyes, mouth, and broken skin. If bitten, wash with soap; apply hydrocortisone or calamine; seek urgent care for severe symptoms; avoid aspirin or ibuprofen until dengue ruled out.

article.articleHeadline: Bloodborne infections: A growing concern for surgeons - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Himachal Pradesh's 2024 data show HBV: 1,469 and HCV: 2,403 laboratory-confirmed cases, with HIV prevalence about 0.06% per NACO. In surgery, patients may test negative in the window period despite infection, so universal infection-control precautions must be applied to every patient. HBV vaccination for healthcare workers is strongly recommended, with post-exposure prophylaxis available if immunity permits. HIV exposure demands immediate PEP, ideally within 72 hours; for HCV there is no vaccine or routine PEP, so early testing and follow-up are essential. Increasing detection of positive markers, including asymptomatic patients, spans emergencies and electives across many specialties. Positive markers should not automatically preclude surgery; instead, identify infection, assess infectivity, optimize patients, and enforce standard PPE, safe sharps, and sterilization. Himachal Pradesh is considering separate theatres, equipment, and protection kits and emphasizes thorough exposure history to gauge window-period risk.

article.articleHeadline: Freezer-free RNA vaccine breakthrough could transform the global fight against emerging diseases

This supports the 100 Days Mission and equitable vaccine access, with involvement linked to India within the broader G7/G20 backing. The platform’s saRNA enables cells to generate additional vaccine RNA copies, potentially reducing starting material, expanding manufacturing capacity, and lowering costs during outbreaks. article.articleHeadline: What can we learn about the next pandemic from the rising flu outbreak?
article.articleSummary: Influenza outbreaks in India show 2–10 times more cases this year across various regions compared with last year. Public guidance emphasizes vigilance without panic, encouraging crowds avoidance, mask use, and vaccination for high-risk groups, alongside ensuring infected individuals receive proper care. Following COVID-19, India maintains robust viral surveillance, with alerts triggered when influenza positivity exceeds a defined threshold. In selected hospitals, severe acute respiratory infection patients exhibit influenza positivity at 16% this year versus 12% last year, highlighting a gap between surveillance and action due to fragmentation among ICMR, NCDC, and state health systems. A unified command structure with clear authority is proposed to coordinate outbreak response. The piece argues that overreaction is preferable to under-response during life-saving scenarios, and that revisiting antiviral use and influenza management guidelines is warranted. It frames epidemics and micro-outbreaks as opportunities to refine response and communication methods for future pandemics.

article.articleHeadline: Ludhiana: Dengue larvae detections drop amid weak monsoon

District epidemiologist Dr. Supreet Kaur attributes the drop in larval detections to less rainfall, though dengue cases remain unchanged: 36 dengue-positive cases reported so far this year, matching the count on the same date last year. She cautions that a higher later-year tally is possible; only 36 cases were reported by September 8 last year, but infections spiked in October–November, yielding 539 cases by December. She blames a week-long sanitation workers’ strike in late July for creating breeding conditions despite reduced rainfall, as garbage accumulation hindered street cleaning.

article.articleHeadline: El Niño puts India on high health-risk radar, says WHO, amid rising dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: El Niño-linked conditions push India into high health-risk category per WHO's Global Public Health Situation Analysis (El Niño 2026, Sept 5). In South Asia, drier, hotter conditions anticipated Aug–Oct. In India, dengue and malaria cases rise in Delhi: August dengue 90 cases, total by Aug 29: 311; malaria July 17 rising to 53 in August, total 119 this year. The WHO notes these vector-borne diseases are not directly caused by El Niño but are affected by it as a risk modifier, influenced by local climate, vulnerabilities, and health infrastructure. Heat stress and temperature surges threaten cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, and metabolic health; effects on pregnant women and newborns, and risks to food security and nutrition. Leptospirosis risk increases with heavy rains and floods, especially where sanitation/drainage is poor. Cross-border displacement at India–Nepal and India–Bhutan borders could spur cross-border transmission.

article.articleSummary: African Swine Fever (ASF) prevention in Taiwan remains stringent as of 2026-09-09. Year-to-date, 588 violations have been recorded, with traveler-carried meat products the largest category; international parcels and mail are also scrutinized. ASF virus can survive about 100 days in pork and up to 1,000 days in frozen meat, with transmission via international travelers carrying meat, cross-border e-commerce parcels, sea-drifted garbage, and animal carcasses. As of August, 134 high-risk parcels were intercepted, with nearly 90% from China and Thailand; among the top source locations, nine of ten have had ASF outbreaks. Fines are heavy: 200,000 TWD for a first offense and 1,000,000 TWD for subsequent offenses. Mid-Autumn Festival gifting raises risk. Agriculture Minister Chen Junji toured the northern Taiwan mail center to urge frontline checks. Taiwan had one ASF case last year; after strict measures, the outbreak was cleared within a month, and WOAH in April affirmed the country’s ASF-free status.

article.articleHeadline: Maps from 74,000 years ago suggest that ancient humans avoided regions where malaria was likely more intense long before agriculture existed.
article.articleSummary: Maps from about 74,000 years ago suggest ancient humans avoided regions with high malaria risk long before agriculture. Malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes shaped prehistoric human ecology across Africa and Eurasia, as researchers reconstructed routes using paleoclimatic models and archaeologic records. Early nomads occupied plateaus where hostile climates prevented pathogen maturation, acting as a thermal barrier that protected hunter-gatherers. Two later climatic windows increased overlap between people and vectors along migratory corridors. The adoption of agriculture and sedentary villages created water resources and deforestation, enabling explosive parasite proliferation near settlements and turning malaria into a persistent Holocene burden. Genomic analyses show intensified immune-defense selection in tropical farming communities, leaving lasting signatures in modern genomes.

article.articleHeadline: Leprosy in Italy, the Spallanzani Institute expert: "A rare disease with seven cases a year, no alarm"
article.articleSummary: Leprosy (Hansen’s disease) remains a rare, well-controlled infection in Italy. In Lazio and nationwide, about seven cases per year are reported, with zero autochthonous transmission since 2003; current cases are imported or involve individuals previously treated, with no infectious load. Mycobacterium leprae is highly transmissible only with prolonged close contact with untreated cases. Symptoms involve skin, eyes, respiratory tract, and peripheral nerves, risking loss of pain sensation. The Spallanzani Institute in Rome acts as the regional reference center for rare infectious diseases since 2005, ensuring diagnostic and therapeutic care. Today, Hansen’s disease is treatable with a three-drug antibiotic regimen for 6–12 months; patients cease to be infectious from the first dose and are monitored thereafter. Globally, cases have fallen about 5.5%; high-endemic countries include Brazil, India, and Indonesia. Italian authorities stress there is no health emergency.

article.articleHeadline: Genetic diversity of Ehrlichia canis revealed in naturally infected
article.articleSummary: Minas Gerais, Brazil—naturally infected dogs in the Unaí microregion, a 27,384-square-kilometer area, exhibit striking genetic diversity of Ehrlichia canis. In nine municipalities, 386 dogs were sampled; initial screening by 16S rRNA PCR identified 38 positives (9.8%), with 21 samples confirmed as E. canis by trp19 PCR (5.4% overall). The study combined two-gene analyses: p28 and trp36, using 21 trp19-positive samples; 12 were p28-positive and eight were trp36-positive. p28 sequences showed 99.27–99.88% nucleotide identity to reference Jake and Jaboticabal strains, but amino acid substitutions at multiple positions indicated meaningful protein variation. Haplotypic analysis revealed nine haplotypes exclusive to Unaí, with haplotype diversity 0.9632, nucleotide diversity 0.0731, and 224 polymorphic sites. Phylogeny based on p28 (30 sequences) split Unaí isolates into two clusters: eight linked to Rio de Janeiro, India, and the United States, and three clustering with Jaboticabal. This points to a mixed, circulating E. canis population in a previously data-poor region.

article.articleHeadline: Genetically edited pigs could be used to defend against African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers at Embrapa are using CRISPR/Cas gene editing to reduce pigs’ susceptibility to African swine fever (ASF). The program aims to create ASF-resistant pigs through targeted genetic changes, initially focusing on SLA-DMA and SLA-DMB genes implicated in pig-virus interactions. Experiments start in vitro with pig fibroblasts; if results are favorable, they may advance to embryos and live animals. The team is also building a dedicated gene-editing platform to support broader pig-health research. This proactive, long-term strategy seeks to fortify the pork industry against future ASF outbreaks, given the disease’s potential for severe economic losses via animal depopulation, trade restrictions, and control measures. Brazil has been ASF-free since the early 1980s, underscoring the emphasis on prevention. The project combines genetic edits with computer analyses to identify gene modifications that alter virus–host interactions, potentially combining multiple edits to further reduce susceptibility.

article.articleHeadline: Chickenpox cases reach 129 in Marataízes and double in less than a month.
article.articleSummary: Chickenpox (varicella) outbreak in Marataízes, Espírito Santo, Brazil, has reached 129 confirmed cases as of August 29, 2026, up from 64 on August 20, 2026, when the municipality declared an alert. Of the 129 confirmed cases, 117 have recovered and 12 remain active; 59 cases are under investigation. The majority of cases are among school students. The municipality emphasizes that the total reflects records accumulated over about two months, not daily incidence, and that active cases are the main metric of current transmission. Epidemiological Surveillance maintains monitoring and continues actions outlined in the Varicella Contingency Plan, coordinating surveillance, health services, vaccination, schools, and communication. Technical notes and workflows were created to guide health services to ensure rapid, organized response, reduce transmission, and prevent new outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Sexual Health in Old Age Requires Prevention and Attention to STIs.
article.articleSummary: Brazil faces a growing public health imperative as aging demographics shift sexual health into geriatric care. Data from Brazil's 2025–2026 National Health Survey (PNS) indicate about 40% of people over 60 remain sexually active. HIV diagnoses among older adults have surged 441% over the past decade, and more than 80% of sexual encounters in this group occur without condom use. The rise of sexually transmitted infections, including syphilis, HIV, gonorrhea, and hepatitis, reflects historical gaps in prevention messaging targeted at seniors. Ageism and silence in clinics hinder diagnosis and treatment, with clinicians often assuming sexuality ends with aging. The article calls for routine inclusion of sexual health in clinical assessments, removing stigma, and providing nonjudgmental, technical conversations about prevention—making condom use a standard component of lifelong healthcare for older adults in Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: International mission evaluates measles control in Bolivia.
article.articleSummary: International mission from PAHO/WHO Regional Monitoring and Verification Commission on measles elimination visits Bolivia Sept 9-11, 2026 to assess actions, epidemiological response, and challenges of the measles outbreak in Santa Cruz and La Paz. The objective is to review progress toward interrupting transmission and strengthen the roadmap for measles elimination. The agenda starts in Santa Cruz with participation from the Ministry of Health and Sports, the Gobernación, OPS/PAHO Bolivia, Inlasa, Cenetrop, Asuss, and the National Immunization Committee. Experts Herminio Hernández (Peru) and Marilda Siqueira (Brazil), together with Bolivian professionals, will analyze 2025–2026 epidemiology with emphasis on the last 12 weeks, sociodemographic profiles, surveillance, laboratory indicators, vaccination coverage, and SRP/SR vaccine availability. On Thursday they travel to La Paz to review seven key aspects: case detection, notification, response, bottlenecks, and enabling factors. Closing on Friday, Elena Vuolo of PAHO/WHO will present final conclusions.

article.articleHeadline: Yellow Fever Keeps Turning Up Outside Traditional Risk Zones and US Travelers Face a Vaccine Timing Problem
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever is turning up outside traditional risk zones. WHO reports 79 human infections in the Americas through May 26, 2026, with wildlife outbreaks signaling forest circulation. In Africa, 16 confirmed cases January–May 2026 and 32 suspected in five other countries. PAHO warns sustained transmission in parts of South America and emergence beyond Amazon hotspots, including São Paulo state, Brazil, and Tolima, Colombia. May 2025 PAHO rated Americas risk high; WHO June 2026 regional risk moderate, global low. Most confirmed cases in 2025–2026 are in unvaccinated people. Last year's tally: 346 cases, 143 deaths across seven countries. In early 2026, 34 cases and 15 deaths were recorded in several nations. Vaccination requires about 10 days for protection; vaccinate at least 10 days before travel at designated clinics; a single dose is generally lifelong; boosters may be considered during ongoing outbreaks; costs vary, and entry may require proof of vaccination.

article.articleHeadline: Sushi lovers may want to put down the chopsticks after study finds alarming number of parasites in tuna
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from the Federal University of Santa Catarina analyzed 53 locally caught skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) and found parasites in 96% of samples. Parasites were detected throughout the fish—intestine, muscle tissue and stomach—with more than 1,400 larvae found in the stomach alone. The study identified two zoonotic parasite genera, Nematoda and Trypanorhyncha, highlighting potential human health risks if ingested. Analyses employed stereomicroscopy, light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy, and the authors stressed that parasites can migrate to edible portions even after processing. They call for rigorous sanitary inspection and immediate evisceration to limit larval spread. Skipjack tuna contributes roughly 58% of global tuna catch and is used in canned tuna and sushi. While many parasitic infections are treatable, consuming raw or undercooked fish can cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea; thorough cooking reduces risk.

article.articleHeadline: Possible outbreak of a respiratory disease is being investigated at a hospital in Linhares.
article.articleSummary: Eight staff members at Hospital Geral de Linhares in northern Espírito Santo, Brazil, report respiratory symptoms as a possible outbreak is investigated. The state health secretariat (Sesa) says representatives from the Centre for Strategic Information and Responses in Health Surveillance (CIEVS), the hospital, and municipal epidemiology met to coordinate the assessment. Causative agent has not yet been identified; samples are being collected for laboratory analysis. The hospital reports active monitoring of symptomatic staff and reiterates preventive measures including hand hygiene, mask use, environmental cleaning, and vigilance of ventilation systems. No ICU patients with similar symptoms, and the hospital continues normal operations. Sesa and the hospital will update measures as the investigation progresses.

article.articleHeadline: Children of Silence: The Inheritance of Leprosy
article.articleSummary: Leprosy, or Hansen's disease, shapes the lives of mothers and their children in this evocative account. Mothers with Hansen's disease endure childbirth amid isolation by midwives, while their babies are adopted by families unaware of their lineage. The Hansenites Movement (Mohan) rises as a demand for recognition, while those left behind mourn a lost bond. The federal government eventually listens, but recognition comes late and pensions cannot replace a mother's embrace or a child's missing years. Today, mothers and their now-adult children seek repair in reunions, confronting intergenerational grief. The piece highlights stigma, family separation, and slow state acknowledgement in the context of Hansen's disease, focusing on longing, belonging, and the pursuit of closure.

article.articleHeadline: During Leprosy Month, the country still has 467 cases under care, reveals the Patronato president, Emma Guzmán.
article.articleSummary: September is Leprosy Month in the Dominican Republic, with about 467 leprosy cases under care nationwide and 63 new cases reported recently, including 3 foreign nationals. The Patronato de Lucha Contra la Lepra, established by decree in 1973, leads public detection, diagnosis, and treatment, with support from the government and the Ministry of Public Health, operating eight centers across the country. Centers are located in Santo Domingo; San Cristóbal; Barahona; San Pedro de Macorís; La Romana; Higüey; Santiago; and Mao in Valverde. Dr. Emma Guzmán, president of the Patronato, notes transmission by contact, prompting focal detection operations to identify clusters. Patient care is free, including travel to centers; treatment typically spans about two years. The country is described as among the nations with the most control and a leading example in detection and treatment, aiming for elimination by 2030, contrasting with higher-burden Brazil and Haiti.

article.articleHeadline: Cases of malaria in Alta Floresta raise alarm over transmission in MT.
article.articleSummary: Five malaria cases in Alta Floresta (Alto Tapajós), Mato Grosso, raise transmission risk in the northern state and Amazonia Legal. Mato Grosso has 1,154 malaria notifications in 2026, up from 986 in all of 2025 (17% higher). Other at-risk MT municipalities include Aripuanã, Colniza, Apiacás, Juruena, and Peixoto de Azevedo. Malaria remains endemic in the Amazon region, which accounts for about 99% of Brazil's cases; this year Brazil totals 65,887, with 63,585 in the Amazon. Amazonas leads with 30,875; Pará 13,650; Roraima 7,015; Rondônia 5,326. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes; symptoms include fever, chills, sweats, headaches, body aches, weakness, nausea, and sometimes vomiting. Prevention emphasizes reducing bites—repellents, long sleeves, bed nets, screened openings—especially near rivers or floating structures; prompt care upon symptoms helps interrupt transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Zambales records 31 cases of leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: Zambales records 31 leptospirosis cases from 4 August to 2 September 2026 amid heavy rainfall and flooding. Subic reports the highest with 15 cases; Cabangan and Castillejos have 3 each; Botolan, San Marcelino, and Sta. Cruz have 2 each; Iba, Palauig, San Felipe, and San Narciso each have 1 case. Of the 31 patients, 23 are male and 8 female. Seven cases are classified as probable, 24 as suspect. Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection caused by Leptospira spirochetes, spread through water, soil, or food contaminated with the urine of infected animals like rodents; flooding worsens transmission by dispersing contaminated urine into standing water and mud.

article.articleHeadline: When staying dry is not an option, how is the government protecting Filipinos from leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis poses a growing threat in flood-affected Philippines as of 2026-09-09. The Department of Health is intensifying community surveillance and outreach to identify people with repeated floodwater exposure and determine eligibility for preventive doxycycline; door-to-door checks by health teams and barangay health workers target daily wage earners, delivery and transport workers, and cleanup crews. Prophylaxis is provided based on exposure frequency, with residents able to access doxycycline through YAKAP clinics and the GAMOT program for consultations and prescriptions. To cope with rising hospitalizations, a leptospirosis tracker monitors bed availability and coordinates patient transfers, moving stable patients to lower-level facilities to reserve major hospitals for those needing intensive treatment, including dialysis. The response blends street-level prevention with in-hospital capacity management, underscoring the urgency for those entering floodwaters to obtain protection and seek early medical advice.

triage.notes: レプトスピラ症は毎年の洪水シーズンにフィリピンで見られる既知の公衆衛生課題であり、保健省が予防投薬・病床管理などの対応を実施中。人-人感染はなく国際的拡大リスクは低いが、入院増加・透析需要など重症化の兆候があるため、続報（症例数・死亡数の推移）を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: DOH steps up leptospirosis response in Pampanga
article.articleSummary: Amid the southwest monsoon (habagat), the Department of Health (DOH) intensified leptospirosis response in Pampanga, ensuring medicines, medical equipment, and hospital readiness. Health Secretary Edwin Mercado and officials visited JBLMGH in San Fernando to review leptospirosis management, establishing a fast lane and dedicated beds, with plans to upgrade equipment for severe cases. Leptospirosis units were inspected as patients were encouraged to seek care. An evacuation center in Bacolor was also visited; families were advised to avoid contaminated floodwater and to take precautions. DOH-CLCHD, in collaboration with DSWD, the Pampanga provincial government, and JBLMGH, reported financial assistance for leptospirosis and dengue patients (as of Sept 3, 76 patients at JBLMGH had received aid). Zero Balance Billing supports medically necessary care. Residents should consult health workers promptly if symptoms arise after floodwater exposure.

triage.headline_ja: DOH、パンパンガ州でレプトスピラ症対応を強化
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の洪水関連レプトスピラ症・デング熱への行政対応であり、国際的拡大リスクは低いが、地域での症例増加と医療体制強化の動きがあるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性の洪水（habagat）に伴うレプトスピラ症・デング熱の増加への保健省の対応報告。国内対応として医療体制強化・財政支援が行われており、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威とは評価されない。

article.articleHeadline: The Philippines approves the first commercial vaccine against swine fever
article.articleSummary: Philippines' Bureau of Animal Industry approves AVAC ASF LIVE, the first commercial vaccine against African swine fever (ASF) for fattening pigs, developed by AVAC Vietnam Joint Stock Company. The lyophilized, attenuated vaccine with inactivated genes is now permitted for public sale to help rebuild the country’s hog industry, which has suffered since ASF first struck in 2019, shrinking the national pig herd from about 13 million to around 8 million. A second vaccine, PROVAC from South Korea, is in BAI trials and could become available next year. ASF outbreaks have reached 76 of 82 provinces, with severe losses among small-scale producers lacking robust biosecurity and the capacity to absorb losses. The move aims to restore production and resilience.

article.articleHeadline: Cardinal David seeks wider access to leptospirosis drugs
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis outbreaks in the Philippines prompt a push for wider access to treatment. Cardinal David urged the DOH, especially DOH-Central Luzon, to verify stock at the barangay level and ensure medicines reach health centers in flooded communities, with easily accessible consultation and prevention points and public notices of where medicines are available. The DOH reports 6,253 leptospirosis cases this year and 22 deaths at San Lazaro Hospital in Manila as of September 7. Officials say 1.2 million doxycycline capsules have been distributed and another 2.6 million are available in regional health centers, but reports on the ground say medicines have run out in some areas. Leptospira bacteria spread via soil or water contaminated by urine from infected animals, including rats, with floodwater serving as a near-perfect transmission vehicle. Emphasize replenishing barangay stocks and timely treatment access.

triage.triage_reason: フィリピンで年間6,253例・死亡22例のレプトスピラ症流行が継続しており、薬剤不足の報告や公的・宗教関係者からの関心の高まりが見られるため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Cebu City dengue response hampered by lack of working spray machines
article.articleSummary: Cebu City's dengue response is hampered by a shortage of functional spray machines, with only one of four DOH-provided rechargeable units working as of Jan–Aug 2026. The city recorded 17 dengue deaths and 634 cases at Cebu City Medical Center (CCMC) from January 1 to August 17, 2026, with August the deadliest month (five deaths). CHD data show cases across numerous barangays, led by Mambaling (35), Labangon (33), Ermita (30), Pasil (29), followed by Tisa (27), Duljo (26), Guadalupe and Quiot Pardo (25), Basak San Nicolas (22), Kalunasan (21), Sawang Calero (20), Lorega (19), Suba Poblacion (18), Pahina Central (17), San Nicolas Central and Talamban (16 each), Calamba and Tejero (15 each). To sustain vector-control efforts and respond to the outbreak, CHD sought about P9.39 million for additional spray machines, supplies, and medicines; the City Council approved P9,392,320 from PAGCOR funds.

triage.notes: デング熱はフィリピンで季節的に発生する風土病だが、当該都市では死亡例・症例数が多く、媒介動物対策の機材不足という管理上の課題が明確に示されている。国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。

article.articleHeadline: Zoomlion disinfects public facilities in Sefwi Wiawso over health risks
article.articleSummary: Zoomlion Ghana Limited conducted a two-day, free disinfection and disinfestation exercise in Sefwi Wiawso Municipality, Western North Region, Ghana, from August 26–27, 2026, to curb vectors and sanitation-related diseases. The efforts ran from 3:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on the first day and resumed 3:30 a.m. to 7:30 a.m. the next day to minimize disruption at key sites including the Sefwi Wiawso Municipal Assembly, markets, lorry parks, public toilets, and refuse container sites. The intervention targets mosquitoes, flies, and other vectors, reducing malaria, cholera, and typhoid risk amid rainy-season flooding. Zoomlion bore the full cost under its Corporate Social Responsibility, offering the service free to the municipality and communities. Local environmental health officials welcomed the effort and urged ongoing sanitation, waste disposal at approved sites, and elimination of standing water to prevent breeding. Collaboration among private sector, local authorities, and communities is emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: Ziro/Bakata: Agricultural VDPs launch an offensive against unsanitary conditions and malaria.
article.articleSummary: On 7 September 2026, agricultural VDPs in Bakata commune, Ziro Province, Burkina Faso, held a sanitation and weed-clearing day across public spaces, including Bakata’s royal courtyard, the Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS), and the VDP offices. Led by Sita Kabré, the volunteers aimed to improve living conditions and public health by removing weeds and standing water that can harbor mosquitoes and fuel malaria transmission. The action reflects the VDPs’ broader role in development and social cohesion beyond farming, with a call for residents to maintain cleanliness of concessions and public spaces to sustain malaria-control gains during this health-priority period.

article.articleHeadline: Malaysia, Indonesia explore digital health, ageing and dengue cooperation, says Health Minister
article.articleSummary: Malaysia and Indonesia are exploring cooperation in digital health, traditional and complementary medicine, healthy ageing and environmental health to address emerging challenges such as zoonotic diseases and dengue. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the discussions occurred during a bilateral meeting with the Indonesian delegation on Sept 9 on the sidelines of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting in Kuala Lumpur. The talks also covered expanding the implementation of the health Memorandum of Understanding signed in Jakarta on July 29 last year. Dzulkefly noted Malaysia's success as a health-tourism destination, generating more than RM2.2 billion in revenue from 968,706 visits in 2025. He said the Madani Government would strengthen health-system resilience through regional cooperation to sustain and improve public health services. The 17th AHMM runs Sept 7–11, 2026, chaired by Malaysia, with Myanmar as Vice Chair, under 'Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems.'

article.articleHeadline: Tragedy in Bangladesh: Measles kills more than 1,000 children.
article.articleSummary: Measles in Bangladesh has escalated since March 2026. By September 9, 2026, health authorities reported 167,580 suspected cases and 19,904 confirmed cases, with 1,002 measles-related deaths—100 laboratory-confirmed, 902 with compatible symptoms. The outbreak heavily affects children, especially under five, across 58 of 64 districts, placing hospitals under strain as 147,393 suspected cases have been hospitalized and 141,819 discharged. The surge follows vaccination gaps and disruptions to immunization programs, enabling rapid spread of this highly contagious virus, and increasing risks of pneumonia and encephalitis. Bangladesh launched an extraordinary measles and rubella vaccination campaign with support from WHO, UNICEF, and Gavi, while aiming to restore routine immunization and locate unprotected children. Cross-border risk with India and Myanmar underscores need for vaccination and surveillance. Preventive emphasis: complete immunization schedules, rapid case detection, and early medical care to reduce transmission.
